items.d: One place to raise an HR request, with routing, SLAs and a visible trail.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Employee HR support is often handled through a combination of emails, calls, messages and basic request tracking. This can result in unclear ownership, inconsistent routing and prioritization, repeated employee follow-ups, limited visibility of request progress, and difficulty measuring HR service performance.

As organizations grow, HR teams need a structured and measurable way to manage employee support requests with clear ownership, service expectations, communication and accountability.

Solution Scope

Evolve the existing PHR Request Tracker into a comprehensive Employee Help Desk / HR Service Management capability.

The solution will provide employees with a single place to raise, communicate about and track HR service requests, while enabling HR teams to route, prioritize, assign, manage and measure requests throughout their lifecycle. The existing Request Tracker should be reused and enhanced wherever possible rather than creating a separate overlapping solution.

Solution List
  • HR Service Catalogue — Categories, Subcategories and Request Types
  • Configurable Request Forms / Templates
  • Handling Groups and Request Routing
  • Assignment and Reassignment
  • Impact, Urgency and Priority Management
  • SLA Profiles, Warnings and Breach Management
  • Configurable Approval Workflows
  • Employee–HR Conversation with Public Replies and Internal Notes
  • Attachments and Request-for-Information flow
  • Employee My Requests and request-status timeline
  • HR Handler Queue / Workbench
  • Request lifecycle management — New to Resolution, Closure and Reopening
  • Lifecycle Notifications
  • Employee Feedback
  • HR Service Dashboards and Analytics

items.d: Approve and act on workflow tasks from WhatsApp, without entering PHR.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Many HR workflows depend on timely actions from managers, supervisors and approvers who may not regularly use PHR. When they need to enter the HR system separately to find and complete individual workflow tasks, approvals can be delayed, requests remain pending, bottlenecks build up, and HR teams spend additional effort sending reminders and following up.

The business need is to reduce avoidable workflow delays by bringing the required task and permitted action closer to the responsible user at the time action is needed.

Solution Scope

Enable authorized users to receive PHR workflow tasks through supported messaging platforms and perform permitted workflow actions directly from that interaction.

The messaging platform acts only as an interaction channel. PHR remains the workflow engine and source of truth, controlling the valid actions, permissions, validations, workflow state and audit history. The initial direction identifies WhatsApp as the first supported platform, with the architecture designed to support additional messaging platforms later.

Solution List
  • Workflow task notifications through supported messaging platforms
  • Initial WhatsApp support with extensible multi-platform architecture
  • Workflow task and recipient identification
  • Secure messaging-user-to-PHR-user identification
  • Existing PHR authorization and organizational-scope enforcement
  • Display of relevant workflow task context
  • Dynamic retrieval of currently valid workflow actions
  • Approve
  • Reject
  • Send Back
  • Request More Information
  • Collection of mandatory comments, reasons or additional information
  • Execution through the existing PHR workflow engine
  • Preservation of existing validations, workflow sequencing and state
  • Validation of expired or changed workflow tasks
  • Workflow action confirmation
  • Workflow audit trail within PHR
  • Notification and action delivery/status tracking

items.d: Ask workforce questions from Teams, WhatsApp or Google Chat.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

C-level and senior management users such as CEOs, CFOs and CHROs frequently need workforce information during business discussions and decision-making, but they may not regularly access PHR or navigate into an HR analytics application.

As a result, workforce intelligence can remain disconnected from the discussions where it is most valuable. Executives may need to switch systems or depend on HR teams to retrieve information for them, slowing decision-making and reducing the practical adoption of workforce analytics.

Solution Scope

Extend the existing PHR AI Insights capability to supported messaging and collaboration platforms so authorized executives can ask workforce-related questions in natural language and receive relevant insights directly within the communication environment they already use.

The messaging platform will act only as an additional interaction channel. AI Insights remains the intelligence and security layer, applying the same data permissions, organizational scope and analytical logic available within PHR.

Solution List
  • AI Insights access through supported messaging platforms
  • Executive workforce questions using natural language
  • Conversational follow-up questions
  • Workforce summaries and management-level analysis
  • Headcount, absenteeism, turnover and other available workforce insights
  • Predictive insights where supported by AI Insights
  • AI-generated recommendations where available
  • Tables, charts or simplified visualizations where supported by the channel
  • Secure messaging-user-to-PHR-user identification
  • Existing AI Insights permissions and organizational-scope enforcement
  • Client-specific data availability enforcement
  • Conversation context and continuity
  • Sensitive workforce information protection
  • Summary responses for complex analytical results
  • Link back to full AI Insights for deeper analysis
  • Reusable architecture for multiple messaging platforms

items.d: One conversational interface across the whole platform, not another module.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

PHR continues to grow with more modules, workflows and capabilities, but users still need to understand where functionality exists, which screens to use and how individual processes work. This creates increasing complexity and limits how easily users can consume the full value of the platform.

Traditional UI-driven interaction also restricts users to the way individual screens and processes have been designed. Activities that involve large volumes of data, multiple steps or repeated transactions can require significant manual effort.

The opportunity is to move beyond screen-based HRIS interaction and enable users to simply tell PHR what they want to achieve, allowing the platform to understand the intent, collect the necessary inputs and securely perform the work on their behalf.

Solution Scope

Establish a single Agentic Platform/interface across PHR where users can naturally communicate with and operate the system.

The target is for the platform to ultimately support any activity an authorized user can perform through the PHR UI, while also enabling new ways of working that are difficult or inefficient through traditional screens.

For example, instead of creating employees individually, a user could upload an Excel file and instruct PHR to create all employees. The platform would interpret the data, apply the relevant PHR configurations and validations, identify issues, obtain confirmation where required and execute the transactions.

The interaction should support more than text, including Excel/CSV files, documents, attachments, images and voice inputs wherever they form part of a PHR activity.

A primary capability of the platform should be user-created Agents, allowing users to create reusable AI workers for their own recurring or specialized activities using the PHR capabilities available to them.

PHR remains the underlying system of record, with existing permissions, organizational access, client configurations, business validations and workflows continuing to govern what can be executed.

Solution List
  • Single Agentic Interface across PHR
  • Natural-language interaction and execution
  • Execution of existing PHR UI capabilities
  • Cross-module and multi-step task execution
  • Bulk operations beyond current UI limitations
  • Excel / CSV-driven transactions and bulk processing
  • File and document-based inputs
  • Attachment submission within applicable transactions
  • Voice-based instructions and submissions
  • Intelligent collection of missing information
  • Existing PHR validation and workflow execution
  • Preview and confirmation for applicable actions
  • Validation-error identification, correction and retry
  • User-created Agents
  • Agent configuration for specific responsibilities and recurring work
  • Reusable Agent execution
  • Role- and permission-aware Agent behaviour
  • Execution history and auditability
  • Extensible foundation for progressively onboarding PHR capabilities

items.d: Heavy reports process in the background while light ones stay instant.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

As client data volumes, reporting periods and report complexity increase, some reports require significantly more processing time than others. When these reports are generated through the same immediate-processing model, users may spend unnecessary time waiting, remain uncertain about report status, submit duplicate requests, and experience reduced confidence in the reporting process.

Resource-intensive reporting can also place additional pressure on application resources and become increasingly difficult to scale as PHR supports larger clients and greater historical data volumes.

Solution Scope

Introduce a hybrid report-generation model within the existing Report Navigator.

PHR should automatically determine the processing load of each report and select the appropriate execution method:

  • Lower-load reports continue to generate immediately.
  • Higher-load reports are generated asynchronously in the background, allowing the user to continue working in PHR.

Once a background report is completed, the requesting user should be notified through PHR and, where applicable, by email with a secure link to View or Download the report.

Report Navigator should remain the primary location for viewing report-processing status and accessing generated reports.

The solution should also define a secure approach for storing, accessing, retaining and removing asynchronously generated report files, including client isolation, report permissions, requesting-user access and secure delivery of generated outputs. The existing proposal already identifies retention, storage implications and security as discovery areas.

Solution List
  • Report processing-load classification / load index
  • Automatic synchronous vs asynchronous execution decision
  • Immediate generation for lower-load reports
  • Background processing for higher-load reports
  • Background report-processing queue
  • Generating / Ready / Failed report statuses
  • Ability to continue using PHR while reports are generated
  • Report completion notification within PHR
  • Email notification for completed background reports
  • Secure View / Download Report link
  • View and download completed reports through Report Navigator
  • Failure reason where available
  • Retry capability for failed report generation
  • Duplicate report-request prevention / warning
  • Report-generation history
  • Secure storage of generated reports
  • Client / tenant isolation of generated files
  • Requesting-user and existing report-permission enforcement
  • Secure link access and expiry rules
  • Report retention and automatic file cleanup
  • Storage management for generated outputs
  • Access / download auditability
  • Handling of permission changes after report generation
  • Report Navigator as the source of truth for report status and completed outputs

items.d: Employee self service through the chat apps people already use.

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Employees frequently need simple HR information or self-service support such as checking leave balances, understanding policies, reviewing attendance information or completing common HR transactions. However, they may still need to open PHR, find the correct module or screen and understand the relevant process.

For occasional HRIS users, this creates unnecessary effort and can lead to continued dependency on HR teams for information and services that are already available through digital self-service.

Solution Scope

Extend the existing Lexi conversational experience to supported messaging platforms, allowing employees to access HR knowledge, retrieve authorized employee information and perform supported self-service transactions through natural conversation.

The messaging platform should act only as another interaction channel. Lexi and PHR remain responsible for understanding the request, collecting required information, applying validations and permissions, executing the transaction and returning the result.

For transactional activities, Lexi should collect all required information, validate the request and present a clear confirmation before making any change in PHR.

Solution List
  • Lexi access through supported messaging platforms
  • Natural-language HR queries and self-service interaction
  • HR policy and document questions
  • Organizational and contextual HR guidance
  • Leave balance and other authorized employee information
  • Attendance information
  • Supported employee self-service transactions
  • Collection of required transaction information
  • Existing PHR validations and business-rule enforcement
  • Transaction preview and confirmation before execution
  • Success / failure response after transaction processing
  • Secure messaging-account-to-PHR-employee identification
  • Existing employee permissions and eligibility enforcement
  • Client-specific configuration and capability controls
  • Sensitive employee-information protection
  • Conversation and session management
  • Session expiry and re-authentication where required
  • Client-level enable / disable controls
  • Control over which Lexi capabilities are exposed externally
  • Transaction and audit history within PHR
  • Extensible architecture for additional supported messaging platforms

items.d: Solution is to accept with SS into clock inputs until the point of punch resolvement then proceed with only HH:MM.

detail.thesis:
1. Problem
  • Biometric devices and WDMS middleware record punches to the second.
  • PeopleHR drops the seconds on import, so two or more punches in the same HH:MM collapse into one.
  • A legitimate punch is silently lost — e.g. an employee moving between adjacent doors/floors within the same minute.
  • Client-visible symptom: "the device log has a punch your system does not show."
2. Guiding principle
  • Seconds are captured and stored as recorded. Calculations stay in minutes.
  • The problem is lost punches, not imprecise minutes.
  • No attendance or payroll threshold anywhere in SL / PH / ID is defined below a minute.
3. Out of scope
  • Device direction (IN/OUT) configuration and misconfigured devices.
  • The break-definition debate ("main door punch-outs should count as break time").
  • Any change to grace, late, OT, no-pay or payroll calculation logic.
  • Any second-level value reaching payroll.
4. Common scope (both modules)
4.1 Capture / storage
  • Import raw clock inputs as-is, seconds included, always — independent of any parameter.
  • Fix the uniqueness key that currently collapses same-minute punches (must include seconds + device).
  • Only biometric device punches carry real seconds. Manual punches, clock in/out widget, mobile and bulk/Excel uploads remain HH:MM, stored with seconds = 00.
4.2 New system parameters (org-wide, same names in both modules)
  • Toggle = No → exactly today's behaviour (seconds dropped, same-minute punches collapse to one).
  • The two filter parameters apply only when the toggle is Yes; greyed out otherwise.
4.3 Filtering rules
  • Repeat-punch filter: punches on the same device AND same direction within N seconds form a group; the first is kept, the rest are ignored for calculation (retained in raw data).
  • Different device = never merged (real access event, audit value).
  • Different direction = never merged.
  • Minimum break filter: break pairs shorter than the configured duration are ignored for calculation (retained in raw data).
  • A manually mapped pair below the minimum gets a warning, not a block.
4.4 Rounding — no new rounding rule
  • Seconds are used only for ordering, repeat filtering, In/Out selection and break pairing.
  • When a punch is fixed against a threshold, its seconds are dropped (08:10:59 → 08:10).
  • This is a precision level, not a configurable rounding option. The existing late/early rounding rule remains the only rounding rule — no back-to-back rounding.
4.5 Execution point
  • All filtering runs at process time, not at import. Raw table stays a faithful copy of the device data.
  • Changing a parameter and re-running the process takes effect with no re-import.
4.6 Activation / reprocessing
  • Turning the toggle on applies forward only. Past days keep processed results until the data process is re-run for those dates.
  • Locked / approved periods untouched.
  • Configuration screen to warn that it should be switched on at the start of an attendance period.
4.7 Visibility of ignored punches
  • Not surfaced in the product UI.
  • Available via database / custom report, as today.
5. Old Attendance module — specific scope
5.1 Processing pipeline

raw clock inputs → resolve Earliest Arrival – Latest Departure window for the assigned shift → repeat-punch filter → first-swipe = In, last-swipe = Out; remaining punches paired as breaks → minimum break filter → drop seconds (HH:MM) → existing threshold evaluation (unchanged)

5.2 Notes / impact
  • No Capture page in this module — no punch-level UI change required.
  • Timesheet and Manual In & Out remain the correction path.
  • Existing In/Out selection logic (first/last swipe in window) is unchanged; it simply operates on a correctly de-duplicated punch set.
  • Break pairing is where the fix has real effect.
  • No change to grace, late, OT, no-pay, midnight crossover or payroll transfer logic.
6. New Attendance module — specific scope
6.1 Processing pipeline

raw clock inputs → resolve Earliest Arrival – Latest Departure window for the shift / each segment → repeat-punch filter → auto-assign thresholds (base mode) / preload existing mapping (unique mode) → minimum break filter → drop seconds (HH:MM) → existing threshold evaluation (unchanged)

6.2 Why the repeat filter matters most here
  • Base mode assigns extreme punches as Shift In/Out and the remainder alternately as Break In / Break Out.
  • A double-tap adds an odd punch and flips the parity of every following break assignment, leaving an unpaired punch and blocking the save (UAC 3.5 / 3.9).
  • Example: 12:00:00, 12:00:01, 12:30:00 → assigned Break Out, Break In, Break Out → last one unpaired.
  • Repeat filter removes one punch → correct 12:00–12:30 break.
  • The minimum break parameter cannot fix this — it removes two punches, preserving parity, so it only handles even-count nonsense pairs.
6.3 Unique mode
  • Same repeat filter applies.
  • Exception: punches in a repeat group carrying different thresholds are all kept (the source treated them as different events).
6.4 UI impact (Attendance Capture page)
  • Punch rows display HH:MM:SS when the toggle is Yes (HH:MM when No), with the existing "+1" cross-day indicator.
  • Recalculated Shift/Segment In-Out bounds continue to display HH:MM (the values used in calculation) — small legend needed to explain the difference.
  • Ignored punches are not displayed. Capture shows processed punches only; filtering is back-end.
  • Manual punch duplicate validation (UAC 5.2): a manual 09:04 against an existing device punch at 09:04:36 is a duplicate and is blocked; message names the existing punch time with its seconds.
  • Mobile Capture (User Story 9) inherits the same behaviour — functional parity.
6.5 Shift change
  • Only punches inside the assigned shift's window reach Capture.
  • On shift change, raw punches are re-evaluated against the new window and the pipeline re-runs.
  • Manual changes are dropped on shift change.
  • Punches matching no shift window: stored, never shown, never evaluated — until a shift change brings them into a window.
7. Open technical questions (input needed for sizing)
  1. Where exactly are seconds dropped today — WDMS→PeopleHR integration, raw punch table key, or the attendance process?
  2. Does every device carry a fixed IN/OUT direction? If any device derives direction by alternating punches, a double-tap flips it and the repeat filter must key on device only for those devices.
  3. Volume/performance impact of process-time filtering on large punch sets.
8. Reference / validation still pending
  • 3–5 real lost-punch cases from eMarketingEye's 78 complaints where the outcome was actually wrong (business validation, not a blocker for sizing).

items.t: OT application by start end time instead of duration

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

In both the old OT application and the new Overtime application, employees apply for OT by entering a duration in the Pre OT and Post OT columns. Customers need to apply for OT as a time window (from and to), so approvers can see exactly when the OT will be worked. A duration alone can't show that, and it can't be checked against the shift's allowed OT windows.

Solution

Setting. Add an OT policy setting: Duration (today's behaviour) or Start and end time. Existing customers stay on Duration.

Applying. Employees enter a from and to time for Pre OT and for Post OT. This applies on web, mobile, apply-on-behalf and bulk upload.

Validation when applying.

  • Pre OT falls between earliest arrival and shift in.
  • Post OT falls between shift out and latest departure.
  • Each window stays within max Pre OT or max Post OT.
  • OT windows on the same day don't overlap, and windows that cross midnight are supported.
  • Flexi shifts: shift out isn't known until the employee punches in, so validate against the widest possible window. If punches already exist, validate against the actual shift in and out.

Processing. Attendance processing pays the lower of the approved OT and the OT actually worked. This settles flexi applications that couldn't be fully checked up front. OT is reprocessed when punches or rosters change.

Screens and reports. Approval screens, notifications and reports show the from and to times.

Both modules. The rules are defined once and built into both the old and new modules.

To confirm

items.t: [GN] Decimal Precision for Contribution Rates in Pa…

detail.thesis:
Problem Space

Organizations manage employee wage-based contributions as part of payroll processing, and the precision required for these contributions can vary depending on statutory requirements, local practices, and organizational policy. For example, Indonesia currently has a requirement to define decimal precision for contribution values, highlighting the need for greater flexibility in managing contribution calculations. At present, there are no separate parameters in the base Payroll module for defining the decimal precision of contributions, either for fixed-amount values or for percentage-based contribution rates.

Without these definitions, organizations cannot control the level of precision applied to contribution amounts and rates, which can lead to rounding inconsistencies, calculation mismatches, and difficulty in meeting organization-specific payroll requirements. Since precision requirements differ from one organization to another, a single fixed behavior is not sufficient.

Solution Scope

Introduce organization-wise contribution decimal definition parameters in the base Payroll module to allow each organization to define the decimal precision applied to employee wage based contributions.

The solution will provide two configurable parameters that govern how fixed-amount contribution values and percentage-wise contribution rates are defined and displayed. These parameters will apply across contribution calculations in the Payroll module, with values maintained at the organization level so that each organization can set its own precision.

Concise List of Items
  • Parameter for fixed amount contribution decimal definition (Eg: if the parameter value is 2, the fixed amount will be presented as 1000.00)
  • Parameter for percentage-wise contribution rate decimal definition (Eg: if the parameter value is 3, the contribution rate will be presented as 52.321%)
  • Organization-wise configuration and maintenance of both parameters
  • Application of the defined decimal precision to employee wage based contributions across the base Payroll module
  • Consistent handling of the defined precision across contribution definition, calculation, and display

Problem Space

BIR Form 1601-C is a statutory remittance return that Philippine employers are required to file. PeoplesHR already generates this report, but only the first page — the second page was excluded because the information it captures is not relevant to an HRIS and has no corresponding data points in the system.

In practice, clients still need the complete form when printing and filing. Because the second page is missing from the generated output, they must source and produce it separately, then manually combine it with the system-generated first page. This creates an extra manual step outside the product, increases the risk of incomplete or mismatched submissions, and results in frequent client requests for the missing page.

Solution Scope

Extend the existing 1601-C report in PeoplesHR to include the government-provided second page as part of the same generated output.

The second page will be reproduced as provided by the Philippine government, with no data points connected or populated. Users will be able to generate the report and receive both pages together, with the second page rendered blank and ready for manual completion where required. The existing report must be reused and extended rather than replaced by a separate output.

All existing data mappings, calculations and data connections on the first page must remain unchanged and continue to function exactly as they do today.

Solution List
  • Addition of the government-provided 1601-C second page to the existing report output
  • Faithful reproduction of the official second-page layout and form structure
  • Blank second page generation with no data binding or population logic
  • Continuity of all existing first-page data mappings, calculations and connections
  • Single-action generation and printing of the complete two-page 1601-C report
  • Consistent pagination, page sizing and print formatting across both pages

Problem Space

Users often search for HR functions using the menu names they are familiar with in their local organization or market. When those familiar names differ from the standard PeoplesHR product menu names, users may be unable to find the correct function even though it already exists in the system.

This creates unnecessary navigation difficulty, especially in localized product instances such as the Philippines where some menu labels differ from the standard product terminology. It can reduce discoverability, increase user confusion, and make Lexi/Search Bar navigation feel less effective.

Solution Scope

Enhance the Search Bar / Lexi navigation capability to support alternative menu names, renamed labels, and market-specific terminology as additional searchable keywords for existing menu items.

When a user searches using an alternative or localized menu name, the system should recognize the keyword and return the corresponding existing menu item without requiring changes to the underlying menu structure.

The initial requirement is driven by the Philippine instance, but the mechanism should be reusable for other markets or clients where alternative terminology is required.

Concise List of Items
  • Support alternative keywords for existing menu items
  • Support renamed/localized menu labels
  • Map multiple keywords to a single existing menu
  • Return the correct menu when users search using familiar local terminology
  • Maintain existing menu navigation and permissions
  • Allow market-specific keyword configuration
  • Initial enablement for Philippine menu terminology
  • Reusable approach for future localization needs
  • Prevent duplicate menu creation solely for search purposes
  • Maintain existing Lexi/Search Bar navigation behavior for standard menu names

Problem Space

HR and business leaders often need external context to properly interpret internal workforce data. Questions around industry benchmarks, labor market trends, workforce practices, compensation trends, and general HR best practices cannot always be answered using an organization’s internal data alone.

Without trusted external context, users may need to leave the HR platform, search across multiple sources, and manually compare external information with their internal insights. This makes the analysis process fragmented and can also introduce concerns around source reliability, transparency, and uncontrolled use of external information.

Solution Scope

Introduce Controlled Web Intelligence within AI Insights to allow external HR, industry, benchmark, and labor-market information to be incorporated into analytical responses where relevant.

The capability should operate under configurable administrative controls, allowing organizations to determine how web-based intelligence can be used. Depending on the configured policy, web intelligence may be disabled, restricted to approved sources, or enabled with clear visibility of the sources used.

External web information should complement internal organizational data rather than replace it, with clear distinction between company-specific insights and externally sourced information.

This should be treated as a future AI Insights enhancement, as web search is not currently part of the existing AI Insights process.

Concise List of Items
  • Web intelligence for HR-related external context
  • Industry and workforce benchmark information
  • Labor market and HR trend information
  • General HR best-practice information
  • Administrator-controlled web intelligence settings
  • Option to disable web intelligence
  • Option to restrict usage to approved sources
  • Option to enable broader web intelligence with source visibility
  • Source references for externally retrieved information
  • Clear separation of internal data and external intelligence
  • Use external information only where relevant to the user’s question
  • Maintain transparency over the origin of external insights
